  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

 Analysis:
As requested by the P&R Commission on August 5, 2020, below is the sequence of
events regarding the recreation department's FY 2019-2020 budget:

1. On November 19, 2019, the Irwindale Community Foundation (ICF) adopted the Fiscal
  Year 2019-2020 budget funding $50,000 to the Recreation Department (Attachment
  "A"). Staff provided the P&R Commission with a verbal report regarding the ICF's
  sponsorship to the Recreation department on December 4, 2019.

2. On March 12, 2020, the City of Irwindale declared an emergency due to the COVID-
  19 global pandemic. Several measures were implemented to reduce the spread of
  COVID-19 including the cancellation of all social gatherings in the City, as well as
  suspending all Library, Recreation, and Senior Center programs. This included the
  suspension of the Parks and Recreation Commission meetings until further notice.

3. On May 13, 2020, the City Council approved adjustments to the Fiscal Year 2019-
  2020 budget due to the COVID-19 Pandemic, including the reallocation of the ICF
  budget for Public Safety costs (Attachment "B").

4. The closure of the Library, Recreation, and Senior Center and cancellation of
  programs for the remainder of the fiscal year resulted in unspent funds allocated by
  the ICF to these departments. On May 19, 2020, the ICF reallocated the unspent
  funds to Public Safety costs in response to the COVID-19 Emergency (Attachment
  "C").

5. On June 24, 2020, the City Council adopted the FY 2020-2021 budget and due to the
  Los Angeles County Department of Public Health Order prohibiting large gatherings;
  no funds were appropriated for events, activities, and programs offered by the
  community services departments.

6. On August 18, 2020, the ICF allocated $144,500 to the recreation department to fund
  the events, activities and programs occurring in FY 2020-2021 (Attachment "D").

7. On September 9, 2020, the City Council considered a resolution to accept a donation
  from the ICF. The Council tabled this matter and directed staff to bring this item
  forward at a future meeting (Attachment "E").

Fiscal Impact:

Approving the ICF donation will make it possible for the recreation department to offer
events, programs, and activities not currently budgeted. The finance department has
prepared a summary of the recreation department's budget for FY 2019-2020 and 2020-
2021, which shows the budget changes made (Attachment "F").

Background and Analysis:

On June 26, 2019 the City Council formally adopted the FY 2019-2020 Annual Budget.
Throughout the fiscal year the City Council also regularly approves additional
appropriations for projects or programs not anticipated at the start of the f!scal year which
are added to the budget. Additionally, on February 12, 2020 approved budget

  Page 1
 adjustments to the FY 2019-2020 Budget as part of the annual Mid-Year Financial
Review, which provided the City Council with the City's financial projections through the
end of the fiscal year at that time.

In a catastrophic turn of events since the Mid-Year Financial Review, the global pandemic
now known as COVID-19 has created a state of emergency at all levels of government.

  l> On March 4, 2020, Governor Newson declared the existence of a state of
  emergency for the State of California due to COVID-19.

  l> On March 13, 2020, the President of the United States declared a national
  emergency in response to the spread of COVID-19.

  l> On March 12, 2020, the City's Director of Emergency Services declared a local
  emergency thereby activating the Emergency Operations Center due to threats to
  people within the City from COVID-19, which threats are likely to be beyond the
  control of the services, personnel, equipment and facilities of the City and will likely
  require the combined forces of the other political subdivisions of the county, state
  and federal government.

The response necessary to stop the spread of COVID-19, which include executive orders
to close nonessential businesses and sheltering al home, has resulted in severe impacts
to the economy. All cities are facing dire financial consequences as a result of COVID-
19, and the City of Irwindale is no exception.

The financial impacts include a significant loss of General Fund revenues, coupled with
increased costs required to implement the necessary measures to stop the spread of
COVID-19 in the community. On March 18, 2020, the City Council held a Special Meeting
ratifying the Proclamation of the Existence of a Local Emergency, and also approved an
appropriation of $1,025,000 from the General Fund Reserves for City's estimated costs
to respond to the COVID-19 Emergency.

Currently, the financial impact to the City's General Fund for FY 2019-2020 is estimated at
$3 million, which includes an estimated loss of revenue of $2 million, and an increase in
expenditures of $1 million. The City is facing significant losses of revenue in some of its
largest revenue sources, which include Sales Taxes, Utility User's Taxes and Mining Taxes.
In order to mitigate the $3 million impact, City Staff conducted a comprehensive financial
analysis of the FY 2019-2020 Budget through the end of the fiscal year.

City Staff will work with the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and the
California Office of Emergency Services (OES) to seek reimbursement of the costs
incurred in responding to the COVID-19 Pandemic throughout the duration of the
emergency. City Staff has also identified alternate revenue sources to help offset some
of the General Fund Revenue losses. Additionally, City Staff has worked closely with City
Departments to review all operating budgets to identify expenditures that can be
suspended or deferred during the current fiscal year.

financial impact, at least through the end of the current fiscal year.

 Date:  August 18, 2020
 To:  Honorable Chairman and Community Foundation Boardmembers
 From:  William K. Tam, Executive Director
 Issue:  Approval of Huy Fong Foods, Inc. Donation and 2020/2021 Budget Allocation

Executive Director's Recommendation:

That the Irwindale Community Foundation approve the donation received by Huy Fong
Foods, Inc., and allocate these funds to the Library, Senior Center, and Recreation
departments, as well as for certain community events and administrative costs for the
2020/2021 fiscal year.

Background:

  1. On July 8, 2020, Huy Fong Foods, Inc. presented the Irwindale Community
  Foundation with a $250,000 donation.

  2. Staff is recommending the distribution of these funds in the following manner:

  Library  $ 28,500
  Senior Citizen Center  $ 59,000
  Recreation  $144,500
  Community Events  $ 11,000
  Administrative Costs  $ 7,000
  Total  $250,000

  3. Due to COVID-19, the events, activities, and programs offered by the three
  Community Services Departments were not funded in the City's Fiscal Year
  2020/2021. Under the current Los Angeles County Department of Public Health
  Order, large gatherings are still not permitted, including the events conducted by
  these departments. Should orders be lifted later in the fiscal year, these funds will
  be essential to restart countless community programs and events.

  4. There are two annual events conducted in the City where a contribution from the
  Irwindale Community Foundation would be appropriate and beneficial. These
  events are the Mayor's State of the City for $7,000, and the Irwindale Young Citizen
  of the Year Competition for $4,000. Due to COVID-19, the format of these events,
  will be conducted virtually. The Mayor's State of the City is anticipated to be held
  in September 2020 and the Irwindale Young Citizen of the Year Competition will

  Page 1
   be held on October 1, 2020. Any unexpended funds for these events will remain
  in the foundation's fund balance for reallocation as needed.

  5. Every year the Irwindale Community Foundation will incur certain administrative
  costs, which include banking fees, audit services, legal services, tax filings, etc. An
  allocation of $7,000 has been earmarked for these administrative costs in FY
  2020/2021.

  6. As a result of the generous donation received by Huy Fong Foods, Inc., it would
  be appropriate at this time for the Irwindale Community Foundation to allocate
  these funds in the manner described above. In doing so, this will allow events,
  activities, and programs to be funded in the 2020/2021 fiscal year.

Fiscal Impact:

This report allocates funding for donations already received in FY 2020/2021. Additional
donations contributed to the Irwindale Community Foundation throughout the fiscal year
will be presented to the Board for direction on future allocations.

  provide valuable community programs and events.

and activities not currently budgeted. This will provide a benefit to the community while
also saving General Fund monies. A budget request itemizing how the corresponding
donations to each department are planned to be utilized will be presented to the City
Council in the near future.
